fact_previews: Qualcomm Eudora was killed off in 2006 amidst shifting corporate priorities.
Eudora OSE replaced Qualcomm Eudora but was not well received and soon died as well.
The code for Eudora was open-sourced and given to the Computer History Museum this year.
Development of Eudora was picked up by a team of C++ programmers led by Nicholas Edward Werner-Matavka.
The program was re-christened Hermes due to legal encumbrances preventing the use of the Eudora name.

fact_previews: Eudora was actually two programs, written in different languages (C and C++) on separate platforms (x86 and Power PC).
One idea is to abandon Macintosh Eudora and to write a Macintosh interface from scratch, using the Windows version's code.
The benefit of using the Windows version's code for the Macintosh interface is that it is economical in respect to time and cost.
The drawback of using the Windows version's code is that Macintosh Eudora users might be unused to the Windows version.
The alternative idea is to open a separate project with the code coming from the Macintosh version.

HERMES Mail/X will support Unicode (UTF-8) and the ability to send messages in every left-to-right alphabetic language.
HERMES Mail/X will include a spelling checker or support the spelling checker included in OS X.
HERMES Mail/X will be a successor to Eudora that will run on all computers with OS X (32-bit and 64-bit).
There will be a stopgap measure between the release of HERMES Mail and Mail/X, allowing users to run the successor to Eudora on their Mac.
